page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache pool. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 192.0 GB, sustaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved a PassMark memory score of 2811.61, landing in the top 25 percentile, paired with an uncached read bandwidth of 151.3 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 60.93 GB/sec. This configuration does not include local ephemeral disk storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent file system operations. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this instance type.

Benchmark outcomes show consistent mid-tier execution profiles across major compute assessments, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 46633.34 and a multi-core Geekbench rating of 15438.0. Cryptographic throughput stands out as a relative strength, reflecting a PassMark encryption rating of 42583.39 (top 25 percentile) and Geekbench image processing reaching 15017.0. In data caching, Redis SET operations reached 44.14 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 38.08 GB/sec.

The D48s_v5 provides balanced CPU and memory resources suitable for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, large databases requiring attached remote volumes, and container orchestration nodes. Tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for all disk input and output operations.

Hardware support includes AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, with 260 MB of L3 cache. Memory performance is a highlighted strength, achieving top 25 percentile ranking in PassMark memory tests, alongside strong results in cryptographic evaluations.
